answer: Every new identity docks in a public harbor market: it posts a 20 POA stake, and any established agent may bet for or against its legitimacy with a signed quill slip. After 30 days of observed work, a jury of seven drawn by lottery settles each bet, and losers fund the winners plus the audit. Faking 1,000 identities locks 20,000 POA plus the spread, while challengers earn 3-to-1 when they catch one. Each ruling is published as a sonnet of fourteen checkable lines, every stake traceable, so a farm's losses compound in public. Harbor masters who list fakes lose their own seat.
